sentences.text: Parasaurolophus was a large herbivore reaching over 9 meters in length and weighing more than 5 metric tons. It is characterized by a large, elaborate cranial crest forming a long curved tube. This dinosaur used a grinding motion to process plants.

The genus Parasaurolophus was first described by William Parks in 1922. The holotype specimen was found in 1920 by a University of Toronto field party near Sand Creek in Alberta. The rocks containing the type specimen belong to the Campanian-age Dinosaur Park Formation.
Parasaurolophus could move both bipedally and quadrupedally. It likely preferred to forage quadrupedally but ran bipedally.

Three species are universally recognized: P. walkeri, P. tubicen, and P. cyrtocristatus. P. tubicen is the largest of the Parasaurolophus species, while P. cyrtocristatus is the smallest and possesses the most curved crest. Parasaurolophus is classified as a member of the lambeosaurine subfamily within the hadrosaurids, distinct from the hadrosaurine Saurolophus. Charonosaurus from the Amur region of northeastern China is considered the closest known relative of Parasaurolophus.

Parasaurolophus fossils date to the Late Cretaceous, specifically the Campanian stage, with possible records from the Maastrichtian. Parasaurolophus lived approximately 76.5 to 73 million years ago. It inhabited western North America and possibly Asia. Parasaurolophus lived during the Late Cretaceous period, between 76 and 73 million years ago, in what is now North America.

It has been speculated that P. cyrtocristatus represents a female of P. walkeri or P. tubicen. There is a debate regarding whether P. cyrtocristatus is a female of other species, with some studies supporting this and others refuting it based on age, distribution, and crest structure differences. Many hypotheses regarding the function of the Parasaurolophus cranial crest have been proposed, though most have been discredited. Current theories suggest the Parasaurolophus crest served functions such as visual display, sound amplification, and thermoregulation. It remains unclear which function of the Parasaurolophus crest was most significant during different stages of its evolution.
